description: Translates human-readable domain names into IP addresses. Uses UDP for standard queries under 512 bytes (or EDNS0) and TCP for zone transfers (AXFR/IXFR) or large query responses.
securityNotes: DNS traffic is plaintext by default. Deploy DNSSEC to prevent cache poisoning, and adopt DoT (DNS over TLS, port 853) or DoH (port 443) for transport privacy.

description: Automatically assigns IPv4 addresses, subnet masks, default gateways, and DNS servers to network clients. Port 67 serves DHCP server listening; Port 68 serves client responses (DORA exchange).
securityNotes: Vulnerable to rogue DHCP servers and DHCP starvation attacks. Mitigate on enterprise switches with DHCP Snooping, Option 82 insertion, and Dynamic ARP Inspection (DAI).

description: Synchronizes computer clocks across packet-switched data networks to millisecond precision using a hierarchical stratum architecture (Stratum 0 atomic reference down to Stratum 1-15 servers).
securityNotes: Accurate time is essential for Kerberos authentication (5-minute maximum skew tolerance), TLS certificate validity, and forensics log correlation. Restrict access to authoritative internal time sources.

description: Monitors network devices, servers, routers, and switches for health metrics, interface statistics, and operational telemetry via Management Information Bases (MIBs) and OIDs.
securityNotes: SNMPv1 and SNMPv2c transmit community strings in cleartext across the wire. Mandate SNMPv3 which provides user authentication (USM) and cryptographic payload encryption (AES).

description: Asynchronous event notifications sent by managed network devices directly to an SNMP management station or NMS when an unsolicited threshold condition or failure occurs (e.g. link down, power supply failure).
securityNotes: Traps can be spoofed on UDP without authentication unless SNMPv3 Inform requests or authenticated trap receivers are configured. Restrict port 162 access via firewall ACLs.

description: Standard architecture for forwarding system event messages, operational logs, and security telemetry from network devices and Unix/Linux servers to central log collectors (RFC 5424).
securityNotes: Standard UDP 514 syslog lacks encryption, sender verification, and delivery guarantees. Adopt Syslog over TLS (RFC 5425, port 6514 TCP) for secure transport to SIEM systems.

description: Encrypted remote command-line login, system administration, SFTP file transfer, and secure port forwarding across untrusted networks.
securityNotes: Disable direct root SSH login, disable password-based authentication in favor of Ed25519/RSA public keys, enforce rate-limiting or fail2ban, and protect management endpoints behind VPN or bastions.

description: Proprietary Microsoft protocol providing interactive graphical desktop access and application virtualization to remote Windows workstations and servers.
securityNotes: Never expose port 3389 directly to the public Internet due to continuous ransomware attacks and brute force campaigns. Enforce Network Level Authentication (NLA), MFA, and access via Remote Desktop Gateway.

description: SOAP-based remote management protocol implemented via the WS-Management standard for remote PowerShell execution and automated Windows administration over plaintext HTTP transport.
securityNotes: Even though Kerberos encrypts message payloads on domain networks over HTTP, WinRM over HTTPS (port 5986) with valid certificates is recommended on untrusted or non-domain segments.

description: Encrypted Windows Remote Management over TLS. Used for secure cross-domain, workgroup, and cloud-to-on-premises PowerShell remoting and automated configuration management (e.g. Ansible).
securityNotes: Requires dedicated TLS listener configuration and server certificate binding. Ensures transport-level encryption regardless of whether domain Kerberos authentication is available.

description: Foundational client-server application protocol for distributing hypertext, web documents, and APIs across the Internet without transport encryption.
securityNotes: All transmitted data, credentials, and session tokens are unencrypted. In production, configure HTTP solely to issue HTTP 301/308 permanent redirects to HTTPS, and enforce HSTS.

description: Standard encrypted web protocol encapsulating HTTP within TLS (Transport Layer Security) to ensure bidirectional confidentiality, integrity, and server authentication.
securityNotes: Mandate modern TLS 1.3 or TLS 1.2 with forward secrecy (ECDHE) ciphers. Disable legacy SSL 3.0, TLS 1.0, and TLS 1.1. Implement automated certificate renewal with ACME.

description: Standard protocol for message transfer between Mail Transfer Agents (MTAs). Relays electronic mail across the Internet from originating MTA to destination mail server.
securityNotes: Port 25 is commonly blocked outbound by residential ISPs and cloud providers to prevent spam botnets. Upgrade opportunistic connections to TLS via STARTTLS, and deploy SPF, DKIM, and DMARC.

description: Dedicated port for Mail User Agents (MUAs like Outlook, Thunderbird) to submit outgoing mail messages to an authorized outgoing mail server with mandatory client authentication.
securityNotes: Mandates SMTP authentication (SASL) and STARTTLS encryption before client credentials or mail payloads are accepted, preventing unauthorized relaying.

description: Implicit TLS mail submission port where the transport session immediately establishes a TLS handshake upon connection before initiating SMTP command sequences.
securityNotes: Recommended by RFC 8314 for end-user mail submission with immediate cryptographic protection, preventing plaintext fallback vulnerabilities.

description: Permits email clients to access and manage messages stored on a remote mail server, supporting multi-device folder synchronization and flag tracking.
securityNotes: Port 143 transmits credentials in plaintext unless the connection immediately upgrades via STARTTLS. Implicit IMAPS (port 993) is strongly preferred.

description: IMAP with implicit TLS encryption from initial socket connection. Standard for mobile and desktop email clients accessing mailbox stores securely.
securityNotes: Provides immediate encryption, ensuring authentication credentials and message bodies remain protected across public and untrusted networks.

description: Legacy mail retrieval protocol where clients download messages from a remote mail server to local storage, typically deleting the remote copies.
securityNotes: Plaintext protocol vulnerable to credential interception. Deprecated in modern enterprise environments in favor of IMAPS or modern Graph/MAPI HTTPS endpoints.

description: POP3 protocol wrapped in implicit TLS from connection initiation, protecting authentication credentials and downloaded messages.
securityNotes: Protects transport credentials, but lacks the modern multi-device synchronization and granular control offered by IMAP and modern cloud mail APIs.

description: Directory query and modification protocol for querying user identities, organizational units, and domain objects in Active Directory and OpenLDAP.
securityNotes: Standard port 389 connections transmit simple bind credentials in cleartext unless SASL signing/sealing or STARTTLS is negotiated. Active Directory mandates signing or LDAPS.

description: LDAP wrapped inside an implicit TLS connection. Required for secure directory authentication, password resets, and user authorization queries across networks.
securityNotes: Ensures all directory queries, attributes, and user credentials remain encrypted. Requires valid enterprise PKI certificates on Domain Controllers.

description: Ticket-based network authentication protocol used by Microsoft Active Directory and MIT Kerberos. Issues Ticket Granting Tickets (TGT) and service tickets to prevent password transmission.
securityNotes: Requires synchronized system clocks across domain members (maximum 5-minute skew by default). Protect Domain Controllers and monitor for Kerberoasting and AS-REP roasting attacks.

description: File sharing, printer sharing, and named pipes remote procedure call (RPC) protocol for Windows enterprise environments and Samba servers.
securityNotes: Block inbound port 445 at the network perimeter. Disable obsolete SMBv1 entirely. Mandate SMB signing and SMB encryption (SMB 3.1.1) to protect against relay and eavesdropping.

description: Storage networking protocol that encapsulates SCSI commands over TCP/IP networks, allowing servers to mount block-level storage targets across IP SANs.
securityNotes: Isolate iSCSI traffic on dedicated non-routable storage VLANs or physical SAN networks. Configure CHAP authentication and utilize IPsec encryption where cross-site transport is required.

description: The standardized exterior gateway routing protocol that manages routing decisions and autonomous system (AS) reachability across the Internet and enterprise cloud interconnects.
securityNotes: Enforce TCP MD5 authentication (RFC 2385) or TCP-AO (RFC 5925), TTL security (GTSM), RPKI route validation to prevent BGP route hijacking, and prefix-lists on peering sessions.

description: Remote Authentication Dial-In User Service (RFC 2865) providing centralized AAA authentication and authorization for 802.1X wireless, switch port security, and VPN access.
securityNotes: RADIUS relies on MD5 and shared secrets which are vulnerable to cryptanalysis. Mandate long random shared secrets, restrict network access, and transition to RadSec (RADIUS over TLS).

description: RADIUS accounting service (RFC 2866) recording session connection duration, byte consumption, and disconnect reasons for auditing and compliance tracking.
securityNotes: Accounting packets contain sensitive user identity and session telemetry. Restrict listener access to authorized network access servers (NAS) via firewalls.

description: Cisco-developed AAA protocol that separates authentication, authorization, and accounting. Used widely for administrator login and per-command authorization on network devices.
securityNotes: Unlike standard RADIUS which only encrypts the password attribute, TACACS+ encrypts the entire packet payload past the 12-byte header using the configured shared secret.

description: Negotiates Security Associations (SA), authenticates peers, and exchanges cryptographic keys for establishing IPsec VPN tunnels (IKEv1 and IKEv2).
securityNotes: Prefer IKEv2 over legacy IKEv1. Enforce strong Diffie-Hellman groups (Group 14+ / 2048-bit or ECDH Groups 19/20) and modern AES-GCM encryption algorithms.

description: Encapsulates IPsec ESP packets inside standard UDP datagrams to permit seamless traversal across Network Address Translation (NAT) gateways and stateful firewalls (RFC 3948).
securityNotes: Allows VPN clients behind residential or enterprise PAT routers to connect securely to corporate concentrators without NAT breakages.

description: Network-layer protocol providing confidentiality, data-origin authentication, connectionless integrity, and anti-replay services for IPsec tunnels. Note: Operates as IP Protocol 50 directly on the IP header, NOT a TCP or UDP port number.
securityNotes: Because ESP has no Layer 4 port numbers, native ESP cannot traverse port-restricted NAT gateways without UDP encapsulation on port 4500 (NAT-T). Ensure firewalls permit IP protocol 50.

description: Network-layer protocol providing connectionless integrity and data authentication for IP packets without data encryption. Note: Operates as IP Protocol 51, NOT a TCP or UDP port number.
securityNotes: AH hashes parts of the IP header (including source and destination IPs). Consequently, any NAT device modifying IP headers will invalidate AH hashes, breaking connectivity.

description: Essential network-layer diagnostic and control protocol used by routers and hosts to generate error notifications (Destination Unreachable, Time Exceeded) and diagnostic probes (Echo Request/Reply for ping). Operates as IP Protocol 1, NOT a TCP/UDP port.
securityNotes: Do not block all ICMP unconditionally! Blocking ICMP Type 3 Code 4 (Fragmentation Needed) breaks Path MTU Discovery (PMTUD), causing subtle packet-dropping black holes for large TCP sessions.

description: Legacy bidirectional interactive text communication protocol developed in 1969 for terminal sessions across ARPANET.
securityNotes: Transmits usernames, passwords, and commands in unencrypted cleartext. Strictly prohibited for production system administration; replace universally with SSH.

description: Legacy client-server file transfer protocol. Port 21 manages control commands and authentication; Port 20 (or dynamic ephemeral ports in Passive mode) handles bulk data transfer.
securityNotes: Transmits user credentials and data payloads in cleartext. Complex dual-port architecture requires firewall helper modules. Replace with SFTP (SSH port 22) or FTPS.

description: Simplified file transfer protocol without user authentication or directory listing. Primarily used for PXE network booting (downloading bootstrap kernels) and network router firmware backups.
securityNotes: Has no authentication, encryption, or integrity mechanisms. Isolate TFTP servers strictly within controlled provisioning VLANs or out-of-band management subnets.

description: Default TCP listening port for Microsoft SQL Server Database Engine instances across enterprise environments.
securityNotes: Never expose database listeners directly to public networks. Enforce TLS encryption for client-server connections and configure Windows Authentication (Kerberos) over SQL logins.

description: Default network listener for open-source MySQL and MariaDB relational database management systems.
securityNotes: Bind the daemon strictly to local interfaces (127.0.0.1) or private VPC subnets. Require TLS connections and avoid root remote login permissions.

description: Default connection port for the PostgreSQL enterprise-class open-source object-relational database system.
securityNotes: Configure pg_hba.conf to enforce scram-sha-256 authentication and reject plaintext connections. Mandate SSL/TLS encryption for all remote client traffic.

description: Network virtualization technology using MAC-in-UDP encapsulation (RFC 7348) to extend Layer 2 overlay segments across Layer 3 underlay datacenter fabrics.
securityNotes: Encapsulates tenant traffic within the datacenter fabric. Protect VTEP endpoints and underlay networks against spoofed UDP injection packets.

description: Modern, lightweight, high-performance VPN protocol using state-of-the-art cryptography (ChaCha20, Poly1305, Curve25519) operating over a single UDP port.
securityNotes: WireGuard is silent by default: it does not respond to unauthenticated packets, mitigating port scanning. Manage private keys securely and rotate endpoint keys periodically.

description: Widely deployed open-source SSL/TLS VPN solution supporting site-to-site and client-to-gateway secure network connectivity.
securityNotes: Default port 1194 UDP is recommended for performance; TCP 443 can be used as fallback for restrictive firewalls. Enforce certificate-based PKI authentication and multi-factor authentication.
